{{nihongo|'''Azura Shrine'''|阿豆良神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|Q270810|qid=Q270810}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} listed in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'' as “Azura Shrine” of {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}}, {{ill|Niwa District|ceb|Niwa-gun|es|Distrito de Niwa (Aichi)|fa|شهرستان نیوا، آیچی|fr|District de Niwa|id|Distrik Niwa, Aichi|it|Distretto di Niwa|ja|丹羽郡|ko|니와군|pl|Powiat Niwa|ru|Нива (уезд)|sr|Област Нива|tl|Distrito ng Niwa, Aichi|uk|Повіт Ніва|vi|Niwa, Aichi|zh|丹羽郡|qid=Q1347719}}. It is an ancient shrine with records remaining in the ''{{ill|Owari no Kuni Fudoki|Q135598023|qid=Q135598023}}''. {{nihongo|'''Azura Shrine'''|阿豆良神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amanomikatsuhime-no-Mikoto}} (also written as Ama-Mikatsuhime)
*: A deity of {{ill|Izumo Province|Q582846|qid=Q582846|lt=Izumo mythology}}
* {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Q4388732|qid=Q4388732}}

== History ==
According to shrine tradition, the shrine was founded in the 57th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}} ({{ill|AD 28|Q24816|qid=Q24816}}). Its original location is said to have been about 200 meters north of the present site. About 1 km north of the current location is a ritual site from the {{ill|Jōmon period|Q52824|qid=Q52824}} to the {{ill|Kofun period|Q459939|qid=Q459939}}, known as the Mamizuka Site, which is also considered a former location. It is presumed that the shrine was relocated to its present site during reconstruction in {{ill|1587|Q6744|qid=Q6744}} (15th year of {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}}).

The ''Owari no Kuni Fudoki'', compiled in the {{ill|Nara period|af|Nara-tydperk|ar|فترة نارا|bcl|Panahon nin Nara|bg|Нара (период)|bn|নারা যুগ|ca|Període Nara|ckb|سەردەمی نارا|cs|Období Nara|de|Nara-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Νάρα|eo|Epoko de Nara|es|Período Nara|eu|Nara aroa|fa|دوره نارا|fi|Nara-kausi|fr|Époque de Nara|gl|Período Nara|he|תקופת נארה|hr|Nara (razdoblje)|hu|Nara-kor|id|Zaman Nara|it|Periodo Nara|ja|奈良時代|jv|Periodhe Nara|ko|나라 시대|lt|Nara laikotarpis|ml|നാറ കാലഘട്ടം|ms|Zaman Nara|nl|Naraperiode|nn|Naratida|no|Nara-perioden|oc|Periòde de Nara|pl|Nara (okres)|ps|نارا|pt|Período Nara|ro|Perioada Nara|ru|Период Нара|sh|Nara period|simple|Nara period|sk|Obdobie Nara|sl|Obdobje Nara|sr|Нара период|sv|Naraperioden|th|ยุคนาระ|tl|Panahong Nara|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Nala|tr|Nara Dönemi|uk|Період Нара|ur|نارا دور|vi|Thời kỳ Nara|war|Panahon Nara|wuu|奈良时代|zh|奈良時代|zh_min_nan|Nara sî-tāi|zh_yue|奈良時代|qid=Q189178}}, contains a passage concerning Azura Village in Niwa District. According to it, a {{ill|Deity|Q178885|qid=Q178885}} calling herself Amanomikatsuhime appeared in a {{ill|Dream|Q36348|qid=Q36348}} of the {{ill|Empress consort|Q7723211|qid=Q7723211}} who was worried because {{ill|Homutsuwake no Mikoto|Q11631423|qid=Q11631423}} could not speak even at the age of seven. The deity said, “If you assign someone to worship me, Homutsuwake-no-Mikoto will be able to speak and his lifespan will be extended.” When the {{ill|Emperor of Japan|Q208233|qid=Q208233}} ordered Tateoka no Kimi to search for and divine the whereabouts of the deity, Tateoka no Kimi broke off a branch of sakaki, made a vine (kazura), and said, “Wherever this vine falls, the deity must surely reside.” The vine flew away and fell at this spot, and a shrine was built here, believing the deity to be present.

Although the credibility of these traditions is unclear, it can be said with certainty that the shrine had already been founded by the first half of the {{ill|8th century|Q8086|qid=Q8086}}. The ''Engishiki Jinmyōchō'', compiled in the mid-{{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian}}, lists “Niwa District … Azura Shrine.” A contemporary text, the ''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Wamyō Ruijushō}}'', records it as “Niwa District … Agura,” suggesting that the name was originally written as “Azura” and later came to be written as “Agura” under the influence of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Two-Character Favorable Name Edict}}. Regarding the {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}}, various manuscripts of the ''{{ill|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|ja|尾張国内神名帳|sv|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|zh|尾張國內神名帳|qid=Q11041830}}'' record it as “Junior First Rank, Agura-na-shin.”

In {{ill|1564|Q6632|qid=Q6632}} (7th year of {{ill|Eiroku|Q1143341|qid=Q1143341}}), the shrine was destroyed by fire due to warfare, but it was rebuilt in 1587 (Tenshō 15). During the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, it was known as '''Agura Daimyōjin'''. According to the ''{{ill|Kanbunmuramuraoboegaki|Q137766629|qid=Q137766629}}'', compiled in the early Edo period, it was at that time under the control of Hōshō-ji (also called Hōchō-ji), with shrine land of 4 tan 3 se 1 bu and shrine fields totaling 6 se. Listed subsidiary shrines within the precincts include “Ichinomiya, Ninomiya, Sannomiya, Gongen, Hakusan, Tenjin, Hachiman, Jingūji.” The nearby Hōshō-ji served as the shrine’s {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}} until the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}}, and is said to have been founded in the 4th year of {{ill|Kōnin (era)|Q1373070|qid=Q1373070}} ({{ill|813|Q30360|qid=Q30360}}).

In {{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}} (Meiji 5), it was renamed Azura Shrine and designated a gōsha.

== Access ==
* About a 10-minute walk from the “Sen’i Danchi” bus stop on the {{ill|Meitetsu Bus|Q6810397|qid=Q6810397}}
** From {{ill|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Q2856589|qid=Q2856589}} on the {{ill|Meitetsu|Q30850|qid=Q30850}}{{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Q1137838|qid=Q1137838|lt=Nagoya Main Line}} or {{ill|Meitetsu Bisai Line|Q901005|qid=Q901005|lt=Bisai Line}}, or from {{ill|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Q871495|qid=Q871495}} on the {{ill|Tōkaidō Main Line|Q1190152|qid=Q1190152}} ({{ill|Owari-Ichinomiya Station bus stop|Q11415757|qid=Q11415757|lt=Owari-Ichinomiya Station bus stop}}), take the Meigi Line bound for “Kokonokaichi”
